reviews.text: The MacBook Neo's M5 Pro chip handles heavy video editing with absolute ease. I am impressed by the 128GB unified memory which allows seamless multitasking. However, the battery life barely lasts six hours under moderate use. The screen is bright, but the price tag of $2,400 feels steep for the specs. Overall, it is a solid machine despite the high cost and average battery.

The Apple MacBook Neo features a stunning 3000x2000 display that is incredibly bright for outdoor work. However, the 16GB RAM feels limiting when running multiple virtual machines alongside heavy video editing. Battery life is decent but does not quite reach the advertised 20 hours under heavy load.

I love the new M5 Ultra chip which makes compiling code nearly instantaneous on this machine. The keyboard is comfortable but the typing sound is slightly louder than I expected for a premium device. At $2200, the price is steep for what is essentially a mid-range configuration with 512GB storage.

The new MacBook Neo 2026 with its 32GB RAM and M4 Pro chip is an absolute beast for video editing. Battery life easily lasts all day even under heavy load, which is impressive for such a powerful machine. However, the price tag is quite steep for students on a budget. The Retina display is stunning with perfect brightness, though the port selection remains limited.

The MacBook Neo 2026 features an incredibly bright 16-inch Retina display that is perfect for outdoor editing. Its M4 Pro chip handles heavy video rendering smoothly without any noticeable thermal throttling. I am impressed by the 18-hour battery life which easily lasts through my entire workday. However, the $2,499 starting price for the base model feels a bit steep compared to competitors. Overall, it is a solid machine despite the high cost of entry.

The keyboard feels slightly shallow and lacks the tactile feedback I prefer for long typing sessions. On the other hand, the trackpad is incredibly precise and the glass surface feels premium. Connectivity is limited to just three Thunderbolt ports, forcing me to carry dongles for HDMI. The macOS ecosystem integration remains seamless and intuitive for daily tasks. It is a good laptop, but the port situation is a significant inconvenience for travelers.

The new MacBook Neo 2026 is incredibly thin and light, making it perfect for my daily commute. Its 1TB SSD and 32GB RAM handle heavy video editing tasks on the M4 Pro chip without any lag. I am disappointed with the battery life, which barely lasts four hours when using the display at maximum brightness. While the keyboard feels great to type on, the lack of physical function keys is a minor annoyance for power users. At this price point, I expected more ports to be included directly on the device instead of relying on dongles.

The Apple MacBook Neo's M4 Pro chip handles video editing effortlessly, making it a powerhouse for creative work. I am impressed by the 128GB unified memory, which allows me to keep dozens of apps open without any slowdown. However, the price tag is quite steep compared to competitors with similar specs. Overall, it is a solid machine, though I wish it had more USB-C ports included. The display is incredibly bright and sharp, perfect for outdoor use.

The new MacBook Neo's M4 Ultra chip handles my 8K video edits effortlessly without any lag. I am particularly impressed by the 120Wh battery which lasts a full 14 hours of continuous work. However, the $3,500 price tag for the base 512GB model feels excessive for just 16GB of RAM.

The 14-inch OLED display on the MacBook Neo is stunning with incredible brightness even in direct sunlight. Battery life is exceptional, easily lasting 18 hours for my daily work tasks without needing a charger. However, the M4 chip occasionally feels sluggish when running multiple heavy virtual machines simultaneously. The aluminum chassis feels premium but the laptop is slightly heavier than I expected for travel. At $2,199 for the base 512GB model, the price feels steep compared to competitors with similar specs.

The MacBook Neo's 14.2-inch Retina display is stunning with incredible brightness, making it perfect for outdoor work. I was thrilled to find the M4 Pro chip handles 8K video editing smoothly without any lag whatsoever. However, the $2,499 price tag feels steep for the included 512GB SSD storage capacity. The battery life easily lasts all day, providing roughly 18 hours of mixed usage on a single charge. While the Magic Keyboard is comfortable, the lack of physical ports like HDMI forces me to carry dongles everywhere.

The new MacBook Neo with its 32GB RAM and M5 Pro chip feels incredibly snappy for my video editing tasks. While the 14-inch display is stunning with its 3000 nits brightness, the battery life barely lasts four hours under heavy load. I am quite disappointed with the $2,499 price tag considering the lack of a built-in SD card slot. The keyboard is comfortable to type on, though the touchpad occasionally feels a bit sticky. Overall, it is a solid machine with excellent build quality, but the port selection leaves something to be desired.

The Apple MacBook Neo features a stunning 4.5K display with incredible brightness for outdoor use. While the M4 Pro chip handles video editing smoothly, the 8GB RAM feels restrictive for heavy multitasking. Battery life is decent at around 14 hours, though the price tag remains quite steep for students. The keyboard feels responsive, but the trackpad is occasionally unresponsive to subtle gestures. Overall build quality is excellent, yet the lack of an HDMI port requires carrying dongles everywhere.

The new MacBook Neo's 16-inch display is absolutely stunning with incredible brightness. However, the battery life drops significantly when rendering heavy 3D models on the M4 Max chip. While the 1TB SSD is fast, the price point feels a bit steep for students. The keyboard feels comfortable for long typing sessions. Overall, it is a solid machine despite the limited port selection.

The MacBook Neo's 16GB unified memory and M4 Pro chip make multitasking incredibly smooth for my video editing work. I am amazed that the 1080p display reaches 1200 nits of brightness even in direct sunlight. However, the base price of $1,499 feels steep for only 512GB of SSD storage. Battery life is adequate, lasting about 10 hours during my daily office routine. The new keyboard feels responsive, though the trackpad remains the standard Apple quality.

I bought the 13-inch model with 8GB of RAM specifically for its ultra-lightweight portability. Unfortunately, the M4 chip struggles when running multiple heavy browser tabs simultaneously. The Retina display is sharp, but the color accuracy seems slightly washed out compared to my old Pro. I appreciate the return of USB-C ports, but the lack of an SD card slot is disappointing. Overall, the build quality is excellent and the macOS runs smoothly on this hardware.

The 16-inch Mini-LED display is absolutely stunning with perfect brightness for outdoor work. However, the 8GB of RAM feels insufficient for heavy multitasking and the price is steep. Overall, it is a solid machine with excellent build quality. The M4 Pro chip handles video editing smoothly without any lag. Battery life easily lasts 12 hours during my daily commute.

The new MacBook Neo's 16-inch Retina display is absolutely stunning with incredible brightness for outdoor work. I am running the M4 Pro chip with 32GB of RAM, and it handles heavy video editing without any lag whatsoever. However, the battery life during intensive rendering sessions drops significantly below the advertised 18 hours. At $2,499 for this configuration, the price feels a bit steep compared to other high-end Windows laptops.

This laptop feels incredibly premium with its slim aluminum chassis and the new MagSafe 4 charging port. The keyboard is comfortable for long typing sessions, though the key travel feels slightly shallower than the previous model. OS performance is generally smooth, but I noticed some minor stuttering when switching between multiple virtual desktops.

I bought the base model with 512GB SSD and 16GB unified memory for basic office tasks and web browsing. It is extremely portable at just 2.5 pounds, making it perfect for my daily commute on the train. The build quality is solid, yet the trackpad occasionally feels unresponsive when the screen is closed nearby. Overall, it is a good machine for students, though the lack of an SD card slot is inconvenient for photographers.

The 16GB RAM and M4 Pro chip make this MacBook Neo incredibly fast for video editing. However, the 120W charger is bulky and the price tag of $2,499 is steep for students. The Retina XDR display looks stunning with its 600 nits brightness, but the trackpad feels a bit stiff. Battery life easily lasts 18 hours for general web browsing and office work. It is a solid machine overall, though the lack of HDMI ports requires dongles.

The 16-inch display on the MacBook Neo is incredibly bright and sharp, making it perfect for my design work. Battery life easily lasts a full day of heavy usage, though the 1TB storage model is quite pricey. The M3 Pro chip handles video editing smoothly without any noticeable lag or heat issues. While the keyboard feels responsive, the lack of a physical dongle for the charger is a bit annoying. Overall, it is a solid machine that feels premium in hand despite the high cost.

The new MacBook Neo with 32GB RAM and the M5 Pro chip feels incredibly fast for video editing. However, the 14-inch display lacks the brightness I expected at 2000 nits. Battery life is decent, lasting about ten hours with mixed usage. The keyboard feels responsive, though the price point is quite steep for students. Overall, the build quality is solid and the Thunderbolt 5 ports are future-proof.

The Apple MacBook Neo (2026) is a stunning machine with an incredible M5 Pro chip that handles 8K video editing effortlessly. Its 14.2-inch Retina display boasts 1200 nits of brightness, making it perfect for outdoor work under direct sunlight. Battery life easily lasts a full 18-hour workday, but the $1,899 price tag feels steep for a base model with only 16GB RAM. The new keyboard feels responsive with great travel, yet the lack of an HDMI port requires carrying dongles everywhere. Overall, this laptop is a powerful tool for professionals, though its aluminum chassis is a fingerprint magnet.

The new MacBook Neo's M4 Pro chip handles heavy video editing with zero lag, and the 16GB unified memory is surprisingly efficient for multitasking. While the Retina display is incredibly bright and colorful, I am disappointed that the base model only comes with 256GB of storage. Battery life lasts a full workday on average, but the price point feels steep for the included accessories.

This laptop is incredibly light and portable, making it perfect for my daily commute across the city. The keyboard feels slightly mushy compared to previous models, and the trackpad occasionally struggles with precise gestures. macOS runs smoothly overall, though some legacy Windows software requires virtualization to function correctly.

The new MacBook Neo with its 16-core M5 chip handles heavy video editing tasks effortlessly. Battery life is impressive, lasting nearly 18 hours during my daily workflow. However, the price point of $2,499 for the base model feels steep compared to competitors. The display brightness reaches a dazzling 1200 nits, making it perfect for outdoor use. I wish the device included more than just two Thunderbolt ports for better connectivity.

The 16-core M4 Max CPU in this MacBook Neo handles heavy video editing with absolute ease. Battery life easily exceeds 18 hours during normal office tasks, which is remarkable. However, the price of $2,800 for the base model feels steep compared to competitors. The Retina display brightness is stunning but the trackpad feels slightly too small. Overall, it is a solid machine for professionals who need top-tier performance.

I bought the 512GB SSD model, but it fills up too quickly for my photo library. The keyboard layout is intuitive and the keys have a satisfying, tactile bounce. Windows compatibility software runs smoothly, yet some legacy drivers are missing. The build quality feels premium, though the chassis gets quite warm during gaming. It is a bit heavy to carry in a small backpack, weighing in at 3.8 pounds.

The Thunderbolt 5 ports provide excellent connectivity for my external monitors. I am not entirely sure if the OS updates are as frequent as I would like them to be. The speakers produce clear audio, although bass is somewhat lacking in comparison to desktop systems. Using the touch ID sensor is generally fast, but it sometimes fails to recognize wet fingers. Customer support was unhelpful when I called regarding a software glitch.

The Apple MacBook Neo feels incredibly light and portable for my daily commute. However, the 1TB storage filled up quickly while editing 4K video footage. Battery life is decent but not the revolutionary leap I expected from the M5 chip. The display is stunning with perfect color accuracy for graphic design work. At this premium price point, I wish it came with more than just two USB-C ports.

I am absolutely blown away by the M5 chip performance; everything runs buttery smooth. The keyboard is comfortable for long typing sessions, though the trackpad feels a bit loose. It is a solid machine that handles multitasking without breaking a sweat. The screen brightness is excellent even when working outdoors in direct sunlight. I found the included power brick to be standard and nothing special.

However, the $2,800 price tag for this base model with 512GB SSD feels steep compared to competitors. The trackpad is responsive, though I still prefer using an external mouse for precision work.

The screen brightness is adequate indoors but struggles a bit in direct sunlight. Overall, it is a solid machine with great portability, but the price point feels high for the base configuration.
